All ten digests resolve against live bytes. ADV-D099-T2-01 landed on Linux and landed on the half of macOS that my own turn-2 NOTE was about: the translation field is now named exactly, and I confirmed against this machine's SDK that P_TRANSLATED is 0x00020000 and that it lives in the kinfo_proc the draft says it lives in. But the macOS arch field in the adjacent item does not. I printed struct kinfo_proc in full from the header: it carries extern_proc and eproc and no cpu_type_t anywhere, so the sysctl the draft names cannot yield the process CPU type it is named to yield. The correct call, proc_pidinfo(T, PROC_PIDARCHINFO) returning struct proc_archinfo, sits in the same header the draft already calls one item earlier — and that item, in turn, names a struct flavor that has no start-time field. The two macOS observations have their APIs crossed.

objections.claim: The macOS process-arch field names `sysctl(CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_PID, T)` -> `kinfo_proc` CPU type. `kinfo_proc` has no CPU type member. The one field on which the accepted ADV-D099-T2-01 repair rests for macOS cannot be read from the API the draft names for it.
objections.why: I did not argue this from memory; I printed the struct. `struct kinfo_proc` in this machine's SDK (`/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk/usr/include/sys/sysctl.h`) is exactly two members: `struct extern_proc kp_proc` and an inline `struct eproc kp_eproc`. I listed every field of both. `extern_proc` carries `p_starttime`, `p_flag`, `p_stat`, `p_pid` and the signal/timing members; `eproc` carries `e_paddr`, `e_sess`, credentials, `e_vm`, `e_ppid`, `e_pgid`, `e_jobc`, tty members, text-size members, `e_flag`, `e_login`, `e_spare`. There is no `cpu_type_t` and no `cpusubtype` in either. `grep -c` for `cpu_type_t|cputype|cpusubtype` over `sys/proc.h` returns 0, and the single hit in `sys/sysctl.h` is outside the `kinfo_proc` definition. So step 5 instructs the implementer to read a member that does not exist. This matters more than a wrong citation because step 5 is fail-closed in both directions: 'Other or unreadable -> reject', and the closing paragraph makes a failed field an invalid job, and invalid jobs are 'replaced, not counted'. Followed literally, every macOS job rejects, and the macos-15 and macos-15-intel arms of G03 and G04 can never accumulate their 21 accepted jobs — the platform whose scarcity OBS-T3-02 exists to record is the platform the contract cannot measure. Followed loosely, the implementer improvises an unreviewed API for the field, which is the precise failure ADV-D099-T2-01 was raised to prevent. The irony is narrow and worth naming: the correct API is already in the header the draft is using. `proc_pidinfo(T, PROC_PIDARCHINFO, ...)` returns `struct proc_archinfo { cpu_type_t p_cputype; cpu_subtype_t p_cpusubtype; }` — flavor 19, declared thirteen lines from the flavor the draft cites in step 4. The draft reaches for `proc_pidinfo` in the step that needs `sysctl`, and for `sysctl` in the step that needs `proc_pidinfo`. I want to be exact about what did land, because most of this repair is right: the *principle* of ADV-D099-T2-01 is honoured on macOS — the field is sampled from T after exec, the parent's own state is excluded by name, the pre-exec helper is excluded by name, and the constants `CPU_TYPE_ARM64` and `CPU_TYPE_X86_64` are real and correctly assigned to the two classes. The translation half of the same repair is not merely right but exactly right, and I verified its numeral. It is the retrieval call for the arch half, and only that, which is wrong.
objections.repair: In step 5, replace the sysctl with `proc_pidinfo(T, PROC_PIDARCHINFO, 0, &ai, PROC_PIDARCHINFO_SIZE)` and read `ai.p_cputype`; keep the accepted values and the reject branches as written. Keep step 6's translation read on the `kinfo_proc` `p_flag`, which is correct as it stands — after this change the two steps use two different calls, which is what the two fields actually require. If a single call is wanted for both, `sysctl.proc_cputype` (via `sysctlnametomib` with the PID appended) is the sysctl-family route to the CPU type, but `PROC_PIDARCHINFO` is the documented flavor and is the smaller change.

objections.claim: The macOS start-identity step names `proc_pidinfo(T, PROC_PIDT_SHORTBSDINFO)` for `tv_sec`/`tv_usec`. `struct proc_bsdshortinfo` has no start-time member. Separately, the value S it records is never compared against anything, so even repaired the step performs no test.
objections.why: Same method, same header. I printed `struct proc_bsdshortinfo` in full: `pbsi_pid`, `pbsi_ppid`, `pbsi_pgid`, `pbsi_status`, `pbsi_comm`, `pbsi_flags`, `pbsi_uid`, `pbsi_gid`, `pbsi_ruid`, `pbsi_rgid`, `pbsi_svuid`, `pbsi_svgid`, `pbsi_rfu`. Thirteen members, no timeval. The 'short' flavor is short precisely because it omits the expensive fields. Start time is available two ways, and the draft is already touching one of them: `struct proc_bsdinfo` (flavor `PROC_PIDTBSDINFO`, 3) has `pbi_start_tvsec` and `pbi_start_tvusec`, and `extern_proc` — that is, `kp_proc` of the very `kinfo_proc` step 5 fetches — has `p_starttime` as a `struct timeval`, which I confirmed at `sys/proc.h:97` with its accessor macro at line 101. So the field the draft wants is inside the struct it is already retrieving one step later. I rate this SHOULD-FIX rather than MUST-FIX for a reason that is worth stating rather than assuming, because it cuts the other way from D099-T3-MF-1. On Linux the starttime pair does real work: S0 is read before exec, S1 after the exec-stop, and S1 != S0 rejects, which is a genuine PID-reuse test. On macOS the process is spawned `POSIX_SPAWN_START_SUSPENDED` and stays suspended until step 8 kills it, so it cannot exit and cannot have its PID recycled while the parent holds it unreaped — the design is already structurally immune to the race S is guarding against. That is why a broken S does not break the measurement the way a broken arch field does. But it also means S is inert twice over: mis-named, and never read again. Nothing in steps 5 through 8 compares S to a second sample, and no reject branch mentions it. Linux states its comparison; macOS records a value and drops it.
objections.repair: Either read start identity from `kp_proc.p_starttime` of the `kinfo_proc` already fetched in step 5 (or `PROC_PIDTBSDINFO`'s `pbi_start_tvsec`/`pbi_start_tvusec`) and state the comparison that makes it operative, or delete step 4 and say plainly that the suspended-and-unreaped child makes PID reuse impossible on this path — which is true, and is a stronger guarantee than the Linux re-read.

notesNonBlocking.observation: '`SIGTRAP` from `PTRACE_O_TRACEEXEC` / TRAPeme' contains a garbled token; the intended word is plainly `PTRACE_TRACEME`, which step 3 sets. The mechanism underneath is sound and I checked it rather than assuming: with `PTRACE_TRACEME` set in the child and no option bits, the kernel delivers a `SIGTRAP` stop to the tracee on successful `execve` and at no earlier point absent an incoming signal, so the `waitpid` really is an exec-completion handshake and not a proxy for one. The `PTRACE_O_TRACEEXEC` alternative the draft offers first is the stricter form but cannot be set until the tracee has already stopped once, so the `TRACEME` path is the one an implementer will use. A one-word typo in a normative clause, recorded rather than raised.

notesNonBlocking.location: Subject, macOS step 3 against Linux step 6
notesNonBlocking.observation: The two platforms bind the digest to the running image with different strength, and the asymmetry is not stated. Linux opens `/proc/T/exe` as an `O_RDONLY` fd and hashes that fd — the kernel hands back the exact vnode the process is executing, so no substitution between check and use is possible. macOS takes `proc_pidpath(T)`, then re-hashes that path by name. Darwin has no fd-to-running-image equivalent, so this is close to the best available, and the draft's 'same inode' qualifier plus the fact that T is suspended and holding the vnode makes a swap detectable rather than silent. I record it because a reader comparing the two protocols will read them as equally strong and they are not, and because the difference is a property of the platform rather than a defect in the draft.
notesNonBlocking.note: Non-blocking. No repair required; a half-sentence acknowledging the asymmetry would be enough if wanted.

objectionNote: I OBJECT with one MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX, and I want to be precise about how narrow the gap is, because nearly everything in this draft holds. My turn-2 MUST-FIX is fully discharged: the ledger is this cycle's and nothing else, each label once, the one predecessor row labelled as a predecessor. My turn-2 NOTE is discharged better than I asked — I said the translation mechanism was left implied, and the draft now names it as T's own kinfo_proc P_TRANSLATED, which I checked against the header and found correct down to the numeral. Every other attack in the dispatch fails: the numerals are D-006's, warm p50 is telemetry and matches exactly which five percentiles D-006 actually bounded, the weekly roll does not suppress the rule, the file-08 edits simulate to 18 of 18 with G13 correctly left unnamed, nothing claims QUALIFIED or SATISFIED, condition 5 stays last, all ten digests resolve, and neither frozen subject moved. What did not land is one API name. Step 5 sends the implementer to kinfo_proc for a CPU type that kinfo_proc does not contain — I printed the whole struct to be sure — while step 4 sends them to a proc_pidinfo flavor for a start time that flavor does not contain. The two macOS steps have their calls crossed, and the correct call for step 5 is declared thirteen lines from the constant step 4 already cites. Because the surrounding text is fail-closed and invalid jobs are replaced rather than counted, the literal reading does not degrade macOS evidence, it makes macOS evidence unobtainable — on the one platform whose scarcity OBS-T3-02 exists to record. This is a two-line repair to a contract I otherwise think is sound, and it is the kind of thing that is far cheaper to fix in the draft than in a harness.
